deliberate_increases.evidence: With the dependency: parity-diff reports 0 capability regressions for both the independence build and the own-entry build against stock ESP-IDF. Without it: 1, persistence.
deliberate_increases.why: Reflex's own key-value store used raw esp_rom_spiflash_* to hold this tier at 1, and that is exactly why it persisted nothing: raw ROM flash access while the CPU executes XIP from the same flash never reaches the medium. The count was protecting a store that silently lost every key it was given — aura pairing impossible, purpose gone by the next boot. Independence measured as subtraction rewarded that; make parity-diff, which measures capability, did not.

measurement_corrections.consequence: The claim that Tier C was clear for the own-entry build was wrong and is retracted. Measured honestly it is 4 there, 8 here. check_independence.py counts externs now, so lowering the number by changing declaration style is no longer possible.
measurement_corrections.what: intr_handler_set / intr_handler_get / intr_handler_get_arg, reached by local extern
measurement_corrections.why: Not a regression — these dependencies were always there and the tool could not see them. It read #include lines only, so anything declared with a local extern was invisible, and this codebase declares symbols that way deliberately for ROM entry points. These three are not ROM: they are ESP-IDF C in components/riscv/interrupt.c, and a comment in reflex_hal_esp32c6.c claimed they lived in mask ROM, which is false. Reflex's allocator registers into ESP-IDF's handler table and reflex_trap_handler reads it to dispatch every interrupt Reflex does not own.

measurement_corrections.consequence: The two configurations now carry separate baselines, because they genuinely have different numbers and a single flat baseline could only be right about one of them. Reported to the user as pre-existing drift when first seen; that was wrong, it was caused by this change and is correct.
measurement_corrections.why: Not a removal. That include sits behind #ifdef REFLEX_OWN_ENTRY, and until the tool could resolve that symbol it counted both branches — so the independence build, which never compiles the include, was charged for it. Reading REFLEX_OWN_ENTRY back from the build's own compile_commands.json resolves it to not-defined there and the include drops out. The same change resolves it to defined for build_own_entry, where the include is real and Tier F is correspondingly 3.

note: Ratchet baseline, per build configuration. Lower is the only legal direction. Regenerate deliberately with tools/check_independence.py --update [--build <dir>].
